strategy.summary: Commit 72802a9 added a third sequential store round trip (productNames) to GET /orders/:id, slowing the `detail` scenario of perf/orders.js: p95 24→34 ms (+42.9%), p99 26→37 ms (+43%), confirmed on rerun. Guard it with scenario-keyed latency thresholds at the baseline plus 20% headroom, and record/file the defect for a person to fix.
inScope: Adding detail-scenario p95/p99 latency thresholds to perf/orders.js (existing thresholds, checks and scenarios kept unchanged)
Recording and filing the detail slowdown
outOfScope: Changing application code to recover the latency
perf/search.js and the list scenario (no confirmed slowdown)
assumptions: Baseline is the median of the last 5 good runs given in the work item (p95 24 ms, p99 26 ms); thresholds are baseline × 1.2: p(95)<28.8, p(99)<31.2.
The app runs for real at BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310); nothing is faked.
Smoke runs (run_tests) use --no-thresholds, so they prove the script runs, not the threshold; the script will fail its thresholds under full load until the app is fixed.

risks.description: Threshold too tight on noisy CI machines (p99 on 200 samples)
risks.mitigation: Uses the run's 20% headroom over the median of 5 good runs, the same rule that flagged the regression.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The detail scenario of perf/orders.js keeps p95 http_req_duration below 28.8 ms (baseline 24 ms + 20%).
The detail scenario of perf/orders.js keeps p99 http_req_duration below 31.2 ms (baseline 26 ms + 20%).

testCases.title: detail scenario holds order-detail latency at its last good level (p95 < 28.8 ms, p99 < 31.2 ms)
steps: Run perf/orders.js: detail scenario requests GET /orders/{1..60} at 20 req/s for 10s
testCases.expected: p(95)<28.8 and p(99)<31.2 for the detail scenario; existing global thresholds unchanged
testCases.rationale: 72802a9 'Show each line's product name on an order' added `await productNames(...)` after orderLines in the GET /orders/:id route: a third sequential store round trip (~6-9 ms each) per request, though orderLines already reads each product and could return the name in the same query. That pushed p95 24→34 ms and p99 26→37 ms.

strategy.environmentNotes: Orders API (npm start) at BASE_URL, default http://localhost:4310.

defects.title: Order detail (GET /orders/:id) slowed ~43% by an extra sequential store query for product names
defects.description: The detail scenario of perf/orders.js should hold its last good latency (median of 5 good runs: p95 24 ms, p99 26 ms; threshold +20%: p95<28.8, p99<31.2). It now measures p95 34 ms (+42.9%) and p99 37 ms (+43%), confirmed on rerun (33/35 ms). The bisect found 72802a9 "Show each line's product name on an order". In src/app.js, the GET /orders/:id route now awaits productNames(...) after orderLines(...). productNames (src/store.js) costs a full store round trip (6–9 ms), so each detail request makes 3 sequential queries instead of 2. orderLines already looks up each line's product to get priceCents, so it could return the name in the same query with no extra round trip.
defects.evidence: k6 run perf/orders.js (full load): ✗ 'http_req_duration{scenario:detail}' p(95)<28.8 → p(95)=33.73ms; ✗ p(99)<31.2 → p(99)=35.46ms. Global thresholds still pass.
